findings.title: Selftest does not check the content of the new dev-run thermal report
findings.detail: thermal_report_from_rows (F6(a) growth, per-die GCI, n_gci_inf, attainable, margin vs twin) is exercised by the selftest only through `sorted(tr) == refs` and `n_layouts_growth_fail == 0`. A version that marks every layout attainable with zero margins, zero +inf GCIs and passes_vs_twin=True leaves the selftest passing (rc 0, no FAIL lines). The function is correct today (my hand check below), but the report feeds the founder's pre-registration decision ('if not attainable on the twin or most candidates, A1 may be unreachable'), so a regression would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Monkeypatched E.thermal_report_from_rows to overwrite attainable/self_margin_K/n_gci_inf/passes_vs_twin/margin_vs_twin_K, then ran E.selftest(): 'M1 rc 0 []'. The offgrid_tj scenario plants +10 K hot candidates whose margin_vs_twin should exceed 2 K, but nothing asserts it.
findings.suggested_check: In offgrid_tj, assert the planted hot fingerprints have passes_vs_twin False and margin_vs_twin_K > 2, and that the twin's self_margin_K equals a hand value.

findings.title: Stack-type signature reads the stack's die/attach thickness, which the solvers do not use; per-die thickness is not part of the type
findings.detail: _stack_signature uses LayerStack.die_attach.thickness and LayerStack.die.thickness. thermal_fem (lines 987-1069) and thermal_layout (263, 286) take die and attach thickness from each Die (d.thickness, d.attach_thickness); the stack's die_attach.thickness is used only for thermal_layout's edge-cell size (line 250). So two references on the same stack whose dies differ only in thickness share a stack type and only one gets the F6(e) spot check. The selftest's 'die attach only' type changes a field the solvers barely use. Ceramic changes such as AlN, the case O003 names, are still caught. The docstring's 'every thermal input of a LayerStack' is literally true, so this is a scope gap, not a wrong result.
findings.evidence: src/moduleforge/geometry/stack.py:138-147 (Die.thickness / Die.attach_thickness are the per-die thicknesses); grep shows thermal_fem.py:987-988,1061-1069 and thermal_layout.py:263,286 read d.attach_thickness/d.thickness.
findings.suggested_check: Add the sorted set of (Die.thickness, Die.attach_thickness) per layout to the signature, or state that stack type excludes per-die thickness.

findings.title: F6(e) spot-check reference is chosen without regard to admissibility
findings.detail: Run.drive sets spot_refs[st] = the first reference of type st in reference order, before and without checking rc.admissible. If that reference is inadmissible, evaluate fails F6e_stack_type_spot_check:<st> and with it the aggregate check, even when a later admissible reference of the same type exists; that reference never gets the FV solves scheduled. A type whose references are all inadmissible contributes nothing to the verdict but still fails the gate. This fails safe (a void run, never a wrong verdict) and cannot happen in the current runner, since nothing sets admissible=False and full() is not implemented.
findings.evidence: e008_run.py:988-989 (spot_refs from all refs) and 1202-1204 (inadmissible gives a failed check, inf).
findings.suggested_check: Pick next(rc for rc in refs if rc.stack_type == st and rc.admissible) and skip types with no admissible reference.

findings.title: Phase B cost range is partly by judgement
findings.detail: All FV cost numbers reproduce exactly from the measurement files, and the model (3.34 h) sits above the second-route estimate (2.37-2.77 h) and above the VM's own level-step exponents (1.04-1.08). The upper bound (exponent 1.28, factor 5.55) is a heuristic, the Mac-to-VM factor was measured on E2 while E008 runs on N2D, and Case 4 was never solved at levels 2-3. The spec states all of this.
findings.evidence: Recomputed: s_mac 5.6134e-6, beta 1.13984, factor 5.104, L1/L2/L3 0.029/0.312/3.341 h, low/high 1.03/6.76 h incl. 0.25 h resize.

findings.title: F6(c) Picard check covers the FV spot checks only implicitly
findings.detail: FV results enter the energy-balance check only. thermal_fv raises RuntimeError on Picard non-convergence at picard_tol 1e-4 K (the gate's value), so a completed FV solve meets the gate. The guarantee depends on the solver's default tolerance, not on a runner check.

findings.title: A NaN energy balance would be dropped by max()
findings.detail: worst_eb = max([worst_eb, *fv_eb]) ignores a NaN that is not first in the list, so a NaN FV energy balance would pass F6c. This is an existing pattern, now applied to the FV values too. Unlikely in practice.
findings.suggested_check: Use a NaN-aware maximum, or check math.isfinite before comparing.
